response.sql: SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg) AS distinct_transactions, COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg)) OVER () AS share FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON tr.transreg = ab.translink JOIN trader t ON t.tradereg = tr.trdref GROUP BY t.tradekind;

assumptions.assumption: Only the existence filter is applied: inner joins require the linked transactionrecord and its trader (via transactionrecord.trdref) to exist. A transaction belongs to exactly one trader, so no transaction is counted in two trader-type groups; COUNT(DISTINCT transreg) handles repeated analyses of the same transaction.
tradekind is nullable, so traders with NULL tradekind form their own group. It is kept as a row and included in the total. The request does not say whether NULL counts as a trader type.

The denominator is the sum of the per-type distinct-transaction counts over all groups (a window SUM over the grouped counts). Multiplying by 1.0 keeps the division non-integer, so the share is unrounded. The SQL targets PostgreSQL, which the JSONB columns suggest.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat a NULL tradekind as not a trader type: drop those traders from the groups and from the total, so the shares sum to 1 across real types only.
alternatives.sql: SELECT t.tradekind, COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg) AS distinct_transactions, COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT tr.transreg)) OVER () AS share FROM advancedbehavior ab JOIN transactionrecord tr ON tr.transreg = ab.translink JOIN trader t ON t.tradereg = tr.trdref WHERE t.tradekind IS NOT NULL GROUP BY t.tradekind;
